{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Online convex optimization with exact separation and per-round query caps\par}\vspace{5pt}


\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{ONX\_\allowbreak{}OCO\_\allowbreak{}SEPARATION\_\allowbreak{}PER\_\allowbreak{}ROUND}



Online learning and bandits



Expected regret for exactly feasible actions on an unknown convex body, with a separately enforced separation budget on each round.



\textbf{Status.} Logarithmic gap; Other quantified gap



\textbf{Gap classes present.} Logarithmic gap; Other quantified gap



\textbf{TASK tags.} solution concept: Unknown domain online regret; task family: Online bandit



\textbf{MODEL tags.} convexity: Convex



\textbf{ORACLE tags.} feedback quality: Exact; operation: Current loss and subgradient; operation: Strong separation certificate; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared; scalar derivative order: Scalar-function first derivative



\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} randomization: Private randomness allowed



\textbf{GUARANTEE tags.} mode: Expectation; quantifier: Algorithm before instance



\textbf{RESOURCE tags.} measure: Q per round; measure: T



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}


Minimize adversarial online convex regret while maintaining exact feasibility in an unknown convex body under a strictly enforced separation-query cap on every round.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}


The unknown compact convex body satisfies \AtlasInlineMath{rB_2^d\subseteq K\subseteq RB_2^d} with public common center zero and public \AtlasInlineMath{0<r\le R}. Set \AtlasInlineMath{\kappa=R/r}; these supplied radii need not be optimal for the individual body.



After the current action, the convex loss may depend on the past and that action. A returned subgradient at the action has norm at most G. The guarantee is uniform over comparators and admissible adaptive loss sequences.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}


Before each action, at most Q calls to an exact strong separation oracle may be made. On any query z in the full Euclidean space, it returns inside if z belongs to K, or a unit vector a satisfying \AtlasInlineMath{\sup_{x\in K}\langle a,x\rangle<\langle a,z\rangle}. The oracle may choose any valid response.



The learner then plays \AtlasInlineMath{w_t\in K} and receives the current convex loss and a subgradient \AtlasInlineMath{g_t\in\partial f_t(w_t)} with \AtlasInlineMath{\|g_t\|\le G}. The upper algorithms use only the subgradient. All preprocessing access to K is charged from round 1; unused calls cannot be carried to a future round. Arithmetic and tests against explicitly stored inequalities are not unknown-body queries.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}


Every played point must be feasible almost surely for every admissible body and every valid separation oracle. Approximate feasibility is not allowed.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}


\AtlasInlineMath{R_T=\sup_{u\in K}\sum_{t=1}^T[f_t(w_t)-f_t(u)]}. The risk is the infimum over almost-surely feasible capped learners of worst-case expected regret over bodies, valid oracle responses, and admissible loss adversaries.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}


The resource is the joint pair (T,Q), where Q is a hard per-round cap rather than an average or total budget; total separation calls are at most QT. One loss/subgradient response is obtained after each action. Internal arithmetic, bit precision, and known-inequality processing are uncharged.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}


All randomized adaptive learners may make full-space separation queries, but must respect the hard cap before each action and be feasible almost surely for every body and valid response rule.




\AtlasMath{\sup_{K,\mathrm{Sep},f_{1:T}}\mathbb E R_T\le r_{\mathrm{reg}}}




Expected regret is taken over learner randomization while feasibility and the query cap hold almost surely on every round.



\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed\_per\_round\_oracle\_cap

\AtlasInlineMath{d}: Euclidean dimension \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d\ge1} integer.

\AtlasInlineMath{r}: Public inscribed-ball radius \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<r\le R}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\kappa}: Public asphericity upper bound \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\kappa\ge1}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\kappa=R/r}



\AtlasInlineMath{Q}: Strict separation-query cap on every round \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{Q\ge1} integer.



\AtlasInlineMath{L_T}: Query reserve for the deterministic fallback \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{L_T\ge1} integer.

\AtlasInlineMath{D_T}: Localization dimension-logarithm scale \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{D_T>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{M=\min\{T,d\}}



\AtlasInlineMath{N_Q}: Truncated dimension divided by the cap \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{N_Q\ge0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{j}: Hidden-facet count in the exact lower bound \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{1\le j\le d-1} integer.



\AtlasInlineMath{\delta_{j,\kappa}}: Normalized hidden-facet comparator advantage \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\delta_{j,\kappa}\ge0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\delta_{j,\kappa}=(\kappa^2-1)/[2\kappa^2(\sqrt{(\kappa^2+1)/(2\kappa^2)}+\sqrt{1+j/\kappa^2})]}



\AtlasInlineMath{a}: Fixed exponent describing the polynomial-in-logarithms budget regime \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{a>0} fixed independently of d,T,kappa,Q.
